slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise 2027 prices where customers stay (mid-market 12%, enterprise at contract terms, established SMB 8%) and activate the promotion cohort instead
Churn is rising because of the 2025 promotion cohort, not because SMB customers have turned against our price
–	Outside the promotion, SMB churn is 2.1%, against 2.0% a year earlier
–	41% of the cohort activated in month one, compared with 72% of others
The CFO's 12% on every plan would add $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M, and hits SMB where Inkwell already wins
–	Renewal timing and caps keep a quarter of the $10.3M out of 2027
–	Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year
A rise can work where customers stay: mid-market, enterprise and SMB customers outside the promotion
–	The mid-market rise pays unless churn more than doubles, to 1.7%
–	8% for established SMB customers nets about $0.7M at 2023's reaction
This mix takes existing customers just past the 15% target; new business must cover a weaker year
–	Existing customers: $99.7M base, $95.6M stress; target $98.9M
–	Five gates, all checked by mid-2027, let us scale the plan back

slides.title: As a result, the mid-market rise pays for itself unless monthly churn more than doubles, to about 1.7%

paragraphs.text: 1 Churn    2 CFO plan    3 Room to price    4 Plan
As a result, the mid-market rise pays for itself unless monthly churn more than doubles, to about 1.7%
Mid-market monthly logo churn at which a 12% rise stops adding ARR, % of customers, 2027
0.9 pp
mid-market monthly logo churn today (H1 2026)
extra monthly churn the rise can absorb: $4.2M added ÷ ($39.0M renewing ARR at the new price × 12 months)
breakeven churn: 2.1 times today's rate
The breakeven rests on four simplifications
▪	Lost ARR in the year ≈ extra monthly churn × 12 months × renewing ARR at the new price (simple, not compounded)
▪	Customers who leave over price are of average size
▪	Expansion from seats and upgrades stays at today's rate; only churn reacts to the rise
▪	Mid-market monthly logo churn starts from its H1 2026 level of 0.8%
1  Breakeven for the rise itself; the 15% growth target is lost much earlier, at about 1.0% a month (gates, last section)
Sources: Palisade Docs briefing pack; team analysis

slides.title: Outside the promotion cohort, an 8% SMB rise would still net about $0.7M if customers react as they did in 2023

paragraphs.text: 1 Churn    2 CFO plan    3 Room to price    4 Plan
Outside the promotion cohort, an 8% SMB rise would still net about $0.7M if customers react as they did in 2023
ARR from an 8% rise for SMB customers outside the 2025 promotion, $ millions, 2027
added: 8% on $16.6M of SMB ARR outside the promotion, all renewing in 2027
lost at the 2023 reaction: churn +0.5 pp for six months, +0.1 pp after (3.6% of ARR)
kept; the rise loses money only if the reaction is 2.1 times 2023's
Why 8%, and why only these customers
▪	8% is the one SMB rise we have measured; 12% would put the plan at $16.80 against Inkwell's $9, and its reaction is unknown
▪	Their churn (2.1% compared with 2.0%) and price complaints (18% compared with 19%) have not moved since 2025
▪	The promotion cohort keeps its price: 52% of its leavers cite price, and most left within two months of the last price step
▪	The extra churn is applied to all of their ARR at the new $16.20 price for twelve months
Sources: Palisade Docs briefing pack; team analysis

Halving SMB churn is out of reach
▪	Best case: the cohort churns like other SMB customers from January, cutting SMB churn from 3.1% to 2.1%, by 32%
▪	Halving SMB churn to 1.55% would need the cohort to churn at 0.56% a month, a quarter of the rate of established SMB customers

▪	Whether the cohort can be activated at all is one of the pack's open questions; the gates track it
